counterfactual_missing_items: multiple intra-articular bodies (would support synovial chondromatosis)
fat signal on T1 (would support osteochondroma)
meniscal tear on MRI (would support lateral meniscus tear)
decisive_items: a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass, with no satellite lesions identified
response.rationale: R1 is the strongest because the lesion invades the tibial plateau and shows peripheral rim enhancement, both characteristic of giant cell tumor. R4 only has internal specks on T2, which is nonspecific and lacks the invasive and rim-enhancing features. Other candidates are contradicted by the absence of fat signal, meniscal tear, or multiple lesions.

rejected.why: Ganglion cyst does not typically invade bone or show peripheral rim enhancement; the T2 internal specks are not characteristic.
Lateral meniscus tear is not supported by the MRI finding of a space-occupying lesion with rim enhancement; clinical findings are nonspecific.
Osteochondroma would show fatty marrow on T1 and be suppressed on fat-sat, but the lesion is isointense to muscle and fat-sat is unremarkable.
Redundant completion of R4 with no additional raw support; adds anatomy but does not address the invasive and rim-enhancing features that favor R1.
